subject: astronomy
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The cosmic microwave background radiation is important because it is:
options: Leftover radiation that is strong evidence for the Big Bang
questions.explain: The CMB is faint radiation from the early universe, a key piece of evidence for the Big Bang.

questions.q: A light-year is a unit of:
questions.explain: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.5 trillion kilometres.

options: In one of the spiral arms, far from the centre
At the edge of the universe
At the exact centre of the Milky Way
questions.explain: The Sun sits in a minor spiral arm roughly halfway out from the galaxy's centre, about 26,000 light-years from the core.

questions.q: The redshift of light from distant galaxies is evidence that the universe is:
questions.explain: Light from distant galaxies is stretched to longer (redder) wavelengths, showing space is expanding.

questions.q: A galaxy with no clear shape or spiral structure is classified as:
questions.explain: Irregular galaxies lack the ordered spiral or elliptical form.

questions.q: The Big Bang theory states that the universe:
options: Began from a hot, dense state and has been expanding ever since
Was created by a collision of two galaxies
questions.explain: The Big Bang describes the universe expanding and cooling from an extremely hot, dense beginning.

questions.q: Elliptical galaxies differ from spiral galaxies in that they:
options: Are rounded or oval with little gas and few new stars
questions.explain: Elliptical galaxies are smooth, rounded collections of mostly older stars with little star formation.

questions.q: Hubble found that more distant galaxies are generally:
questions.explain: Hubble's law states recession speed is proportional to distance, supporting an expanding universe.

questions.q: Which of these is the largest in scale?
questions.explain: A galaxy contains billions of stars and their systems, far larger than a single solar system.

questions.q: The Milky Way is broadly classified as what type of galaxy?
questions.explain: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy with arms winding out from a central bulge.

questions.q: In the formation of a planetary system, the planets form from material in the:
options: Protoplanetary disc of gas and dust around the young star
questions.explain: Planets grow by accretion of dust and gas within the flat protoplanetary disc orbiting the new star.

questions.q: Stars and planetary systems form from collapsing clouds of gas and dust called:
questions.explain: A nebula collapses under gravity to form a star, surrounded by a protoplanetary disc.
